Net revenue difference-in-means test for randomized experiments

Source: R/net_revenue.R
net_revenue_test.Rd

net_revenue_test() analyzes net revenue in a randomized experiment without ever counting order rows as customers. Given a customer cohort (treatment assignment and exposure time), a table of paid orders, a table of (possibly partial) refunds, one common cutoff time, and a fixed observation window, it builds exactly one net-revenue value per mature customer and feeds those values through infer's native difference-in-means, permutation, and p-value machinery.

A customer is mature when their entire observation window is observable at the cutoff, i.e. exposure + window <= cutoff. Only mature customers enter the test. Mature customers with no qualifying orders are retained with a net revenue of zero, so the comparison is customer-level rather than an analysis of purchasers only. Immature customers are returned separately and never analyzed.

For each mature customer, only paid orders in the half-open window [exposure, exposure + window) are counted. Net revenue subtracts the refunds recorded on or before cutoff that belong to those counted orders. Refunds are first aggregated to the order level, so several partial refunds on one order can never multiply the order's contribution. All monetary inputs are whole numbers of cents.

The point estimate is the difference in mean net revenue, treatment minus control. The permutation distribution is generated by permuting the group label across customers, which preserves both group sizes; orders are never permuted and purchasers are never analyzed on their own. The reported p-value is two-sided.

Usage

net_revenue_test(
  customers,
  orders,
  refunds = NULL,
  cutoff,
  window,
  exposure = "exposure",
  group = "group",
  customer_id = "customer_id",
  order_id = "order_id",
  order_time = "order_time",
  order_amount = "order_amount",
  refund_id = "refund_id",
  refund_order_id = "order_id",
  refund_time = "refund_time",
  refund_amount = "refund_amount",
  treatment = NULL,
  control = NULL,
  reps = 1000,
  seed = NULL
)

# S3 method for class 'net_revenue_test'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

customers

A data frame with one row per customer. Must contain the customer key, the assigned group, and the exposure time.

orders

A data frame with one row per paid order. Must contain the order key, the customer key, the order time, and the paid amount.

refunds

A data frame with one row per refund, or NULL when there are no refunds. Must contain the refund key, the order key, the refund time, and the refund amount. Refunds recorded after cutoff are ignored when computing net revenue, but every refund, regardless of timestamp, must reference an existing order.

cutoff

A single time: the common as-of time at which order and refund data are considered complete.

window

The fixed observation window, as a difftime or (for Date and POSIXct times) a positive number of days. It is applied relative to each customer's exposure.

exposure, group, customer_id

Column names in customers giving the exposure time, the assigned group, and the customer key.

order_id, order_time, order_amount

Column names in orders giving the order key, the order time, and the paid amount (whole cents).

refund_id, refund_order_id, refund_time, refund_amount

Column names in refunds giving the refund key, the refunded order key, the refund time, and the refund amount (whole cents).

treatment, control

Optional strings naming the treatment and control levels of group. If only one is supplied, the other is inferred from the two observed levels. If neither is supplied, group must be a factor and its level order is used (the first level is treatment). The estimate is always treatment minus control.

reps

A positive whole number: the number of permutation replicates.

seed

Optional single number used to seed the permutation step. The rest of the computation is deterministic.

x

A net_revenue_test result.

...

Unused.

Value

A list of class net_revenue_test with elements:

  • estimate: observed difference in mean net revenue (cents), treatment minus control.

  • null_distribution: a tibble with columns replicate and stat (cents), the permutation distribution from generate() and calculate().

  • p_value: the two-sided permutation p-value from get_p_value().

  • customers: one row per mature customer, with the counted order count, gross revenue, refunds, and net revenue (all in cents).

  • immature_customers: one row per customer whose window extends past cutoff; these are excluded from the test.

  • orders: the order-level attribution detail, including whether each order was counted and its net contribution.

  • groups: the treatment and control labels and the number of mature customers in each.

  • reps, cutoff, window: the settings used.

See also

calculate(), generate(), get_p_value()

Other wrapper functions: chisq_stat(), chisq_test(), observe(), prop_test(), t_stat(), t_test()

Examples

customers <- data.frame(
  customer_id = c("c1", "c2", "c3", "c4", "c5"),
  group = factor(
    c("treatment", "treatment", "control", "control", "treatment"),
    levels = c("treatment", "control")
  ),
  exposure = as.Date(c(
    "2024-01-01", "2024-01-02", "2024-01-01", "2024-01-03", "2024-01-20"
  ))
)

orders <- data.frame(
  order_id = c("o1", "o2", "o3", "o4"),
  customer_id = c("c1", "c1", "c3", "c2"),
  order_time = as.Date(c(
    "2024-01-02", "2024-01-03", "2024-01-02", "2024-01-02"
  )),
  order_amount = c(5000, 2500, 4000, 1000)
)

refunds <- data.frame(
  refund_id = c("r1", "r2"),
  order_id = c("o1", "o1"),
  refund_time = as.Date(c("2024-01-04", "2024-01-05")),
  refund_amount = c(1000, 500)
)

net_revenue_test(
  customers, orders, refunds,
  cutoff = as.Date("2024-01-31"),
  window = 14,
  reps = 100,
  seed = 1
)
#> Net revenue difference-in-means test
#>   Groups: treatment = treatment, control = control
#>   Mature customers: 4 (treatment 2, control 2)
#>   Immature customers (excluded): 1
#>   Observed mean difference: 1500 cents (treatment - control)
#>   Permutation reps: 100
#>   Two-sided p-value: 0.62
